text: Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS complying with the definition of paragraph 2.1 shall, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, meet the performance requirements of paragraphs 5.1 and 5.3 to 5.6 of this Regulation.
condition: when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges

text: Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS submitted to approval for the Car to car scenario shall, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, meet the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.1.
condition: vehicle submitted to approval for Car to car scenario

text: Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS submitted to approval for the Car to pedestrian scenario shall, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, meet the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.2.
condition: vehicle submitted to approval for Car to pedestrian scenario

text: Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS submitted to approval for the Car to bicycle scenario shall, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, meet the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.3.
condition: vehicle submitted to approval for Car to bicycle scenario

text: The effectiveness of the AEBS shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields.

The electromagnetic immunity of the AEBS shall be demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements and respecting the transitional provisions of the 06 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
Conformity of the AEBS with the safety aspects of electronic control systems shall be shown by meeting the requirements of Annex 3.
In addition to the collision warnings, the AEBS shall provide the driver with the appropriate warnings specified in paragraphs 5.1.4.1 to 5.1.4.3.
The AEBS shall provide the driver with a failure warning when there is a failure in the AEBS that prevents the requirements of this Regulation from being met.
condition: when there is a failure in the AEBS that prevents the requirements of this Regulation from being met

text: The AEBS failure warning shall be as specified in paragraph 5.5.4 (constant yellow optical warning signal).
There shall not be an appreciable time interval between each AEBS self-check.
In the case of an electrically detectable failure, there shall not be a delay in illuminating the AEBS failure warning signal.
condition: in the case of an electrically detectable failure

text: Upon detection of any non-electrical failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment), the AEBS failure warning signal as defined in paragraph 5.1.4.1 shall be illuminated.
condition: upon detection of any non-electrical failure condition

text: If the AEBS has not been initialised after a cumulative driving time of 15 seconds above a speed of 10 km/h, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver.
condition: if the system has not been initialised after a cumulative driving time of 15 seconds above 10 km/h

text: The information that the AEBS has not been initialised shall exist until the system has been successfully initialised.
A deactivation warning shall be given when the AEBS is deactivated.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a means to deactivate the AEBS

text: The AEBS deactivation warning shall be as specified in paragraph 5.4.3.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a means to deactivate the AEBS

text: Subject to the provisions of paragraphs 5.3.1 and 5.3.2, the AEBS shall provide emergency braking interventions described in paragraphs 5.2.1.2, 5.2.2.2 and 5.2.3.2 having the purpose of significantly decreasing the speed of the subject vehicle.
condition: subject to driver interruption provisions of paragraphs 5.3.1 and 5.3.2

text: The AEBS shall be designed to minimise the generation of collision warning signals in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision.
condition: situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision

text: The AEBS shall be designed to avoid advanced emergency braking in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision.
condition: situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision

text: False reaction avoidance shall be demonstrated in the assessment carried out under Annex 3, and this assessment shall include in particular the scenarios listed in Appendix 2 of Annex 3.

Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS shall meet the performance requirements of UN Regulation No. 13-H in its 01 series of amendments for vehicles of Category M1 and N1 or Regulation No. 13 in its 11 series of amendments for vehicles of Category N1.

Any vehicle fitted with an AEBS shall be equipped with an anti-lock braking function in accordance with the performance requirements of Annex 6 to UN Regulation No. 13-H in its 01 series of amendments or of Annex 13 to UN Regulation No. 13 in its 11 series of amendments.

When an imminent collision with a preceding vehicle of Category M1 in the same lane is detected with a relative speed above that speed up to which the subject vehicle is able to avoid the collision (within the conditions specified in paragraph 5.2.1.4.), the AEBS shall provide a collision warning as specified in paragraph 5.5.1.
condition: car to car scenario approval; imminent collision detected with relative speed above the avoidable speed

text: In the car to car scenario the collision warning shall be triggered at the latest 0.8 seconds before the start of emergency braking.

In case the collision cannot be anticipated in time to give a collision warning 0.8 seconds ahead of an emergency braking, a collision warning shall be provided as specified in paragraph 5.5.1. no later than the start of emergency braking intervention.
condition: car to car scenario; collision cannot be anticipated in time for a 0.8 s warning

text: The car to car collision warning may be aborted only if the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present.
The car to car collision warning shall be tested according to paragraphs 6.4. and 6.5.
When the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision with a preceding vehicle, there shall be a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s² to the service braking system of the vehicle.
Higher deceleration demand values than 5 m/s² are permitted during the collision warning only for very short durations, e.g. as haptic warning to stimulate the driver's attention.

The car to car emergency braking may be aborted or the deceleration demand reduced below 5.0 m/s² only if the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present or the risk of a collision has decreased.
The car to car emergency braking shall be tested in accordance with paragraphs 6.4. and 6.5.
The car to car AEBS shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 10 km/h and 60 km/h and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.
condition: car to car scenario approval; not deactivated as per 5.4

text: In absence of driver's input which would lead to interruption according to paragraph 5.3.2., the AEBS shall be able to achieve a relative impact speed that is less or equal to the maximum relative impact speed shown in the tables of paragraph 5.2.1.4.
condition: no driver interruption; road flat, horizontal, dry with good adhesion; weather not affecting dynamics (no storm, not below 0°C); tyres and brakes properly operational; no severe uneven load; no trailer and mass between maximum mass and mass in running order; illumination at least 1000 Lux, no extreme sensor blinding; target not extreme in RCS or shape; no significant weather affecting sensing; no overhead obstructions; preceding M1 vehicle unobstructed, clearly separated, constantly travelling or stationary; centre planes displaced not more than 0.2 m; straight travel, not turning at an intersection

text: When conditions deviate from those listed in paragraph 5.2.1.4., the AEBS shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy.
condition: conditions deviate from those listed in 5.2.1.4

text: The behaviour of the AEBS in conditions deviating from those listed in paragraph 5.2.1.4. shall be demonstrated by the manufacturer in accordance with Annex 3, and may, if deemed justified, be followed by testing by the Technical Service in deviating conditions.
The rationale for and the results of verification testing in deviating conditions for the car to car scenario shall be appended to the test report.
condition: if verification testing in deviating conditions is performed

text: The car to car speed reduction shall be demonstrated according to paragraphs 6.4. and 6.5.
At the request of the manufacturer an N1 vehicle may be assessed according to the requirements for α >1.3 regardless of its α value (α = Wr/W × L/H).
condition: at the request of the manufacturer

text: For relative speeds between the listed values, the maximum relative impact speed assigned to the next higher listed relative speed shall apply; for masses above the mass in running order, the maximum relative impact speed assigned to the maximum mass shall apply.

Car to car, M1, stationary/moving target: at relative speeds of 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40 km/h the maximum relative impact speed shall be 0.00 km/h at maximum mass and 0.00 km/h at mass in running order.
Car to car, M1: at a relative speed of 42 km/h the maximum relative impact speed shall be 10.00 km/h at maximum mass and 0.00 km/h at mass in running order.
Car to car, M1: at a relative speed of 45 km/h the maximum relative impact speed shall be 15.00 km/h at maximum mass and 15.00 km/h at mass in running order.

Car to car, M1: at a relative speed of 60 km/h the maximum relative impact speed shall be 35.00 km/h at maximum mass and 35.00 km/h at mass in running order.

For relative speeds between the listed values, the maximum relative impact speed assigned to the next higher listed relative speed shall apply; for masses above the mass in running order, the maximum relative impact speed assigned to the maximum mass shall apply.

Car to car, N1: at a relative speed of 55 km/h the maximum relative impact speed shall be 35.00 km/h at maximum mass and 30.00 km/h at mass in running order.
Car to car, N1: at a relative speed of 60 km/h the maximum relative impact speed shall be 40.00 km/h at maximum mass and 35.00 km/h at mass in running order.

When the AEBS has detected the possibility of a collision with a pedestrian crossing the road at a constant speed of 5 km/h (within the conditions specified in paragraph 5.2.2.4.), a collision warning shall be provided as specified in paragraph 5.5.1. no later than the start of emergency braking intervention.
The car to pedestrian collision warning may be aborted only if the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present.
When the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision with a pedestrian, there shall be a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s² to the service braking system of the vehicle.
Higher deceleration demand values than 5 m/s² are permitted during the pedestrian collision warning only for very short durations, e.g. as haptic warning.

The car to pedestrian emergency braking may be aborted or the deceleration demand reduced below 5.0 m/s² only if the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present or the risk of a collision has decreased.
The car to pedestrian emergency braking shall be tested in accordance with paragraph 6.6.
The car to pedestrian AEBS shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 20 km/h and 60 km/h and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.
condition: car to pedestrian scenario approval; not deactivated as per 5.4

text: In absence of driver's input which would lead to interruption according to paragraph 5.3.2., the AEBS shall be able to achieve an impact speed with a pedestrian that is less or equal to the maximum impact speed shown in the tables of paragraph 5.2.2.4.
condition: no driver interruption; pedestrians unobstructed and perpendicularly crossing with lateral speed not more than 5 km/h; road flat, horizontal, dry with good adhesion; weather not affecting dynamics (no storm, not below 0°C); tyres and brakes properly operational; no severe uneven load; no trailer and mass between maximum mass and mass in running order; illumination at least 2000 Lux, no extreme sensor blinding; no significant weather affecting sensing; no overhead obstructions; single pedestrian with human silhouette and movement; impact point displaced not more than 0.2 m from centre plane; straight travel, not turning at an intersection; unambiguous object separation

text: When conditions deviate from those listed in paragraph 5.2.2.4., the AEBS shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy.
condition: conditions deviate from those listed in 5.2.2.4

text: The behaviour of the AEBS in conditions deviating from those listed in paragraph 5.2.2.4. shall be demonstrated by the manufacturer in accordance with Annex 3, and may, if deemed justified, be followed by testing by the Technical Service in deviating conditions.
The rationale for and the results of verification testing in deviating conditions for the car to pedestrian scenario shall be appended to the test report.
condition: if verification testing in deviating conditions is performed

text: The car to pedestrian speed reduction shall be demonstrated according to paragraph 6.6.

When the AEBS has detected the possibility of a collision with a bicycle crossing the road at a constant speed of 15 km/h (within the conditions specified in paragraph 5.2.3.4.), a collision warning shall be provided as specified in paragraph 5.5.1. no later than the start of emergency braking intervention.
The car to bicycle collision warning may be aborted only if the conditions prevailing a collision are no longer present.

The AEBS shall provide the means for the driver to interrupt the collision warning.
The AEBS shall provide the means for the driver to interrupt the emergency braking.

Interruption of the collision warning and of the emergency braking may be initiated by any positive action (e.g. kick-down, operating the direction indicator control) that indicates that the driver is aware of the emergency situation.

The vehicle manufacturer shall provide a list of the positive actions that interrupt the collision warning and emergency braking to the technical service at the time of type approval, and it shall be annexed to the test report.
The AEBS function shall be automatically reinstated at each initiation of the powertrain.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the AEBS function

text: A new engine start (or run cycle) performed automatically, e.g. by the operation of a stop/start system, shall not be considered an initiation of the powertrain, so it shall not be relied on as the reinstatement event.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the AEBS function

text: The AEBS control shall be designed in such a way that manual deactivation of the AEBS is not possible with less than two deliberate actions.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the AEBS function

text: The AEBS control shall be installed so as to comply with the relevant requirements and transitional provisions of UN Regulation No. 121 in its 01 series of amendments or any later series of amendments.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the AEBS function

text: It shall not be possible to manually deactivate the AEBS at a speed above 10 km/h.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the AEBS function

text: The vehicle manufacturer shall provide to the technical service at the time of type approval a list of situations and corresponding criteria where the AEBS function is automatically deactivated, and it shall be annexed to the test report.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the AEBS function

text: The AEBS function shall be automatically reactivated as soon as the conditions that led to the automatic deactivation are not present anymore.
condition: if the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the AEBS function

text: Where automatic deactivation of the AEBS function is a consequence of the driver manually switching off the ESC function of the vehicle, this deactivation of the AEBS shall require at least two deliberate actions by the driver.
condition: if automatic deactivation of the AEBS results from the driver manually switching off the ESC function

text: A constant optical warning signal shall inform the driver that the AEBS function has been deactivated; the yellow failure warning signal specified in paragraph 5.5.4 may be used for this purpose.
condition: if the AEBS function has been deactivated

text: While automated driving functions are in longitudinal control of the vehicle (e.g. ALKS is active) the AEBS function may be suspended or its control strategies (braking demand, warning timing) adapted without indication to the driver only as long as it remains ensured that the vehicle provides at least the same collision avoidance capabilities as the AEBS function during manual operation.
condition: while automated driving functions are in longitudinal control of the vehicle

text: The collision warning referred to in paragraphs 5.2.1.1, 5.2.2.1 and 5.2.3.1 shall be provided by at least two modes selected from acoustic, haptic or optical.

A description of the warning indication and the sequence in which the collision warning signals are presented to the driver shall be provided by the vehicle manufacturer at the time of type-approval and recorded in the test report.
Where an optical means is used as part of the collision warning, the optical signal may be the flashing of the failure warning signal specified in paragraph 5.5.4.
condition: where an optical means is used as part of the collision warning

text: The failure warning referred to in paragraph 5.1.4.1 shall be a constant yellow optical warning signal.

Each AEBS optical warning signal shall be activated either when the ignition (start) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or when the ignition (start) switch is in a position between the "on" (run) and "start" position that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position (initial system (power-on)).
condition: does not apply to warning signals shown in a common space

text: The AEBS optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight.
The satisfactory condition of the AEBS optical warning signals must be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.

When the driver is provided with an optical warning signal to indicate that the AEBS is temporarily not available (e.g. due to inclement weather conditions), the signal shall be constant; the failure warning signal specified in paragraph 5.5.4 may be used for this purpose.
condition: when an optical warning signal indicates that the AEBS is temporarily not available

text: At a Periodic Technical Inspection, it shall be possible to confirm the correct operational status of the AEBS by a visible observation of the failure warning signal status following a "power-ON" and any bulb check.
Where the failure warning signal is in a common space, the common space must be observed to be functional prior to the failure warning signal status check.
condition: if the failure warning signal is shown in a common space

text: At the time of type approval, the means chosen by the manufacturer to protect against simple unauthorised modification of the operation of the failure warning signal shall be confidentially outlined; alternatively, this requirement is fulfilled when a secondary means of checking the correct operational status of the AEBS is available.
The AEBS tests shall be performed on a flat, dry, concrete or asphalt road affording good adhesion.
The test surface shall have a consistent slope between level and 1 per cent.
The ambient temperature during the AEBS tests shall be between 0°C and 45°C.
The horizontal visibility range shall allow the target to be observed throughout the test.
The AEBS tests shall be performed when there is no wind liable to affect the results.
Natural ambient illumination must be homogeneous in the test area.
Natural ambient illumination must be in excess of 1000 lux for the car to car scenario tests.
Natural ambient illumination must be in excess of 2000 lux for the car to pedestrian scenario tests.
Natural ambient illumination must be in excess of 2000 lux for the car to bicycle scenario tests.
It should be ensured that AEBS testing is not performed whilst driving towards, or away from the sun at a low angle.

Tests may be conducted under deviating test conditions (e.g. not dry surface, below the specified minimum ambient temperature) only at the request of the manufacturer and with the agreement of the Technical Service, whilst the performance requirements are still to be met.
condition: at the request of the manufacturer and with the agreement of the Technical Service

text: The vehicle shall be tested at the mass in running order with an additional mass of maximum 125 kg, including the measuring equipment and a possible second person, to demonstrate compliance with the requirements referring to the mass in running order.
The vehicle shall be tested at the maximum mass.
The load distribution shall be according to the manufacturer's recommendation and be annexed to the test report.
No alteration to the vehicle load shall be made once the test procedure has begun.
During the series of test runs, the fuel level may decrease but shall never fall below 50 %.

If requested by the vehicle manufacturer, the vehicle can be driven a maximum of 100 km on a mixture of urban and rural roads with other traffic and roadside furniture to initialise the sensor system.
condition: if requested by the vehicle manufacturer

text: If requested by the vehicle manufacturer, the vehicle can undergo a sequence of brake activations to ensure the service brake system is bedded in prior to the test.
condition: if requested by the vehicle manufacturer

text: If requested by the vehicle manufacturer, the average temperature of the service brakes on the hottest axle, measured inside the brake linings or on the braking path of the disc or drum, is between 65 and 100°C prior to each test run.
condition: if requested by the vehicle manufacturer

text: Details of the pre-test condition strategy requested by the vehicle manufacturer shall be identified and recorded in the vehicle type approval documentation.
condition: if pre-test conditioning is requested by the manufacturer

text: The mounted tyres shall be identified and recorded in the vehicle type approval documentation.
The vehicle may be fitted with protective equipment only if it does not affect the results of the tests.

The target used for the vehicle detection tests shall be a regular high-volume series production passenger car of Category M1 or alternatively a soft target representative of a passenger vehicle in terms of its identification characteristics applicable to the sensor system of the AEBS under test according to ISO 19206-3:2021.
The reference point for the location of the target vehicle shall be the most rearward point on the centreline of the vehicle.

The target used for the pedestrian detection tests shall be a child articulated soft target representative of the human attributes applicable to the sensor system of the AEBS under test according to ISO 19206-2:2018.

The targets used for the bicycle detection tests shall be a soft target representative of the bicycle with an adult cyclist attributes applicable to the sensor system of the AEBS under test according to ISO 19206-4:2020.
Details that enable the test target(s) to be specifically identified and reproduced shall be recorded in the vehicle type approval documentation.

In the stationary vehicle target test, the subject vehicle shall approach the stationary target in a straight line for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with a subject vehicle to target centreline offset of not more than 0.2 m.
In the stationary vehicle target test, the Technical Service may, if deemed justified, test any other speeds listed in the tables in paragraph 5.2.1.4 and within the speed range of paragraph 5.2.1.3.
condition: if deemed justified by the Technical Service

text: The functional part of the stationary vehicle target test shall start with the subject vehicle travelling at the required test speed within the tolerances and lateral offset prescribed, at a distance corresponding to a TTC of at least 4 seconds from the target.
In the stationary vehicle target test, the tolerances shall be respected between the start of the functional part of the test and the system intervention.

In the moving vehicle target test, the subject vehicle and the moving target shall travel in a straight line, in the same direction, for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with a subject vehicle to target centreline offset of not more than 0.2 m.
In the moving vehicle target test, the target shall travel at 20 km/h with a tolerance of +0/-2 km/h.
In the moving vehicle target test, the Technical Service may, if deemed justified, test any other speeds for subject vehicle and target vehicle within the speed range of paragraph 5.2.1.3.
condition: if deemed justified by the Technical Service

text: The functional part of the moving vehicle target test shall start with the subject vehicle travelling at the required test speed within the tolerances and lateral offset prescribed, at a distance corresponding to a TTC of at least 4 seconds from the target.
In the moving vehicle target test, the tolerances shall be respected between the start of the functional part of the test and the system intervention.

In the pedestrian target test, the subject vehicle shall approach the impact point with the pedestrian target in a straight line for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with an anticipated subject vehicle to impact point centreline offset of not more than 0.1 m.

The functional part of the pedestrian target test shall start with the subject vehicle travelling at the required test speed within the tolerances and lateral offset prescribed, at a distance corresponding to a TTC of at least 4 seconds from the target; the tolerances shall be respected between the start of the functional part and the system intervention.

The pedestrian target shall travel in a straight line perpendicular to the subject vehicle's direction of travel at a constant speed of 5 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h, starting not before the functional part of the test has started.

The pedestrian target's positioning shall be coordinated with the subject vehicle such that the impact point on the front of the subject vehicle is on the longitudinal centreline of the subject vehicle with a tolerance of not more than 0.1 m, if the subject vehicle would remain at the prescribed test speed and not brake.
In the pedestrian target test, the Technical Service may, if deemed justified, test any other speeds listed in the table in paragraph 5.2.2.4 and within the speed range of paragraph 5.2.2.3.
condition: if deemed justified by the Technical Service

text: From the start of the functional part until the subject vehicle has avoided the collision or passed the impact point with the pedestrian target, there shall be no adjustment to any control of the subject vehicle by the driver other than slight steering adjustments to counteract any drifting.
The pedestrian test shall be carried out with a 6-year old child pedestrian soft target as defined in paragraph 6.3.2.

The assessment of the impact speed in the pedestrian test shall be based on the actual contact point between the target and the vehicle, taking into account the vehicle shape without additional protective equipment permitted per paragraph 6.2.4.

In the bicycle target test, the subject vehicle shall approach the impact point with the bicycle target in a straight line for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with an anticipated subject vehicle to bicycle crankshaft impact point centreline offset of not more than 0.1 m.

The functional part of the bicycle target test shall start when the subject vehicle is travelling at a constant speed at the required test speed within tolerances and lateral offset, the bicycle target is travelling at its required test speed within tolerances, and the distance corresponds to a TTC of at least 4 seconds from the collision point/target.
In the bicycle target test, the tolerances shall be respected between the start of the functional part of the test and the system intervention.

The bicycle target shall travel in a straight line perpendicular to the subject vehicle's direction of travel at a constant speed of 15 km/h +0/-1 km/h, starting not before the functional part of the test has started.
During the acceleration phase of the bicycle prior to the functional part of the test, the bicycle target shall be obstructed.

The bicycle target's positioning shall be coordinated with the subject vehicle such that the impact point on the front of the subject vehicle is on the longitudinal centreline of the subject vehicle with a tolerance of not more than 0.1 m, if the subject vehicle would remain at the prescribed test speed and not brake.
In the bicycle target test, the Technical Service may, if deemed justified, test any other speeds listed in the table in paragraph 5.2.3.4 and within the speed range of paragraph 5.2.3.3.
condition: if deemed justified by the Technical Service

text: From the start of the functional part until the subject vehicle has avoided the collision or passed the impact point with the bicycle target, there shall be no adjustment to any control of the subject vehicle by the driver other than slight steering adjustments to counteract any drifting.
The bicycle test shall be carried out with a bicycle soft target as defined in paragraph 6.3.3.
The assessment of the impact speed in the bicycle test shall be based on the actual contact point between the target and the vehicle, taking into account the vehicle shape.

For the failure detection test, an electrical failure shall be simulated, e.g. by disconnecting the power source to any AEBS component or any electrical connection between AEBS components, without disconnecting the electrical connections for the failure warning signal of paragraph 5.5.4 or the optional manual AEBS deactivation control of paragraph 5.4.1.
With a simulated failure, the failure warning signal of paragraph 5.5.4 shall be activated and remain activated not later than 10 s after the vehicle has been driven at a speed greater than 10 km/h.
The failure warning signal shall be reactivated immediately after a subsequent ignition "off" ignition "on" cycle with the vehicle stationary as long as the simulated failure exists.
In the deactivation test, after turning the ignition switch to "on" and deactivating the AEBS, the deactivation warning signal of paragraph 5.4.3 shall be activated.
condition: for vehicles equipped with means to manually deactivate the AEBS

text: After turning the ignition switch to "off" and again to "on", the previously activated deactivation warning signal shall not be reactivated, indicating that the AEBS has been reinstated as specified in paragraph 5.4.1; if ignition is by key, this shall be fulfilled without removing the key.
condition: for vehicles equipped with means to manually deactivate the AEBS

text: Each test scenario (one test setup at one subject vehicle speed at one load condition of one category) shall be performed two times; if one of the two runs fails, the test may be repeated once, and the scenario is passed if the required performance is met in two test runs.
The number of failed test runs shall not exceed 10.0 per cent of the performed test runs for the Car to Car tests.
The number of failed test runs shall not exceed 10.0 per cent of the performed test runs for the Car to Pedestrian tests.
The number of failed test runs shall not exceed 20.0 per cent of the performed test runs for the Car to Bicycle tests.
The root cause of any failed test run shall be analysed together with the Technical Service and annexed to the test report.

If the root cause of a failed test run cannot be linked to a deviation in the test setup, the Technical Service may test any other speeds within the speed ranges defined in paragraphs 5.2.1.3, 5.2.1.4, 5.2.2.3, 5.2.2.4, 5.2.3.3 or 5.2.3.4 as relevant.
condition: if the root cause cannot be linked to a deviation in the test setup

text: During the assessment as per Annex 3, the manufacturer shall demonstrate, via appropriate documentation, that the system is capable of reliably delivering the required performances.

Virtual testing may be used by request of the vehicle manufacturer as an alternative for some of the tests described in paragraphs 6.4. to 6.7. only if the virtual testing is verified and validated according to Annex 4 and used in accordance with Annex 4.
condition: if virtual testing is requested by the vehicle manufacturer

text: Virtual testing may be used in the evaluation of the warning and activation tests in accordance with paragraph 1.8. of Schedule 3 and Schedule 8 of Revision 3 of the 1958 Agreement.

Where virtual testing is used, at least 30 per cent of required tests shall be performed physically, including at least one test of each scenario variant described in paragraphs 6.4 to 6.7 relevant for the approval, to demonstrate that the complete physical system can reliably deliver the required performance.

The physical tests to be performed shall be agreed between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service; tests already performed as part of the model validation and corresponding to the vehicle type approval can be considered as part of the 30 per cent of required tests.

In the case of modification of the vehicle type and extension of the approval according to paragraph 7, the proportion of physical tests required to demonstrate that the complete physical system continues to reliably deliver the required performance may be less than 30 per cent of the required tests and shall be agreed between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service.
condition: in the case of modification of the vehicle type and extension of approval where virtual testing is used

text: Where virtual testing is used by the manufacturer, a separate report including at least the additional information specified in Annex 4 shall be annexed to the test report.
condition: where virtual testing is used by the manufacturer

text: Procedures concerning conformity of production shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
A vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements of paragraph 5.

The Type Approval Authority which has granted approval may at any time verify the conformity of control methods applicable to each production unit; the normal frequency of such inspections shall be once every two years.

If the holder of the approval completely ceases to manufacture a type of vehicle approved in accordance with this Regulation, he shall so inform the Type Approval Authority which granted the approval.
condition: if production of the approved vehicle type is definitively discontinued

text: Upon being informed that production is definitively discontinued, the Type Approval Authority shall forthwith inform the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
condition: if production of the approved vehicle type is definitively discontinued

text: The approval mark affixed to the vehicle shall be arranged according to the model of Annex 2, with the dimension a not less than 8 mm.
The approval mark shall be marked with C for Car to Car, P for Car to Pedestrian and B for Car to Bicycle according to the scenarios approved.
Annex 3 shall apply to the safety aspects of complex electronic vehicle control systems and to safety related functions identified in this Regulation which are controlled by electronic system(s).

The information disclosed to the Technical Service shall show that "The System" respects, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in this Regulation and that it is designed to operate in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.
The transmission links to and from overriding systems/functions outside of the scope of this Regulation shall be included in the complex electronic vehicle control system.

The manufacturer shall provide a documentation package which gives access to the basic design of "The System" and the means by which it is linked to other vehicle systems or by which it directly controls output variables.
The function(s) of "The System" and the safety concept, as laid down by the manufacturer, shall be explained.
Documentation shall be brief, yet provide evidence that the design and development has had the benefit of expertise from all the system fields which are involved.
For periodic technical inspections, the documentation shall describe how the current operational status of "The System" can be checked.

The Technical Service shall assess the documentation package to show that "The System" is designed to operate, under non-fault and fault conditions, in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.

The Technical Service shall assess the documentation package to show that "The System" respects, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in this Regulation.
The Technical Service shall assess the documentation package to show that "The System" was developed according to the development process/method declared by the manufacturer.

The formal documentation package for the approval, containing the material listed in paragraph 3 (with the exception of that of paragraph 3.4.4.), shall be supplied to the Technical Service at the time of submission of the type approval application and shall be used as the basic reference for the verification process of paragraph 4.

The Technical Service shall ensure that the formal documentation package remains available for a period determined in agreement with the Approval Authority, of at least 10 years counted from the time when production of the vehicle is definitely discontinued.
The additional material and analysis data of paragraph 3.4.4. shall be retained by the manufacturer and made open for inspection at the time of type approval.

The manufacturer shall ensure that the additional material and analysis data remains available for a period of 10 years counted from the time when production of the vehicle is definitely discontinued.

A description shall be provided which gives a simple explanation of all the control functions of "The System" and the methods employed to achieve the objectives, including a statement of the mechanism(s) by which control is exercised.
Any described function that can be over-ridden shall be identified and a further description of the changed rationale of the function's operation provided.
condition: if a described function can be over-ridden

text: A list of all input and sensed variables of "The System" shall be provided and the working range of these defined.

A list of all output variables which are controlled by "The System" shall be provided, with an indication in each case of whether the control is direct or via another vehicle system, and the range of control exercised on each such variable shall be defined.
Limits defining the boundaries of functional operation of "The System" shall be stated where appropriate to system performance.
A list shall be provided collating all the units of "The System" and mentioning the other vehicle systems which are needed to achieve the control function in question.
An outline schematic showing the units of "The System" in combination shall be provided with both the equipment distribution and the interconnections made clear.
The function of each unit of "The System" shall be outlined and the signals linking it with other units or with other vehicle systems shall be shown.

Interconnections within "The System" shall be shown by a circuit diagram for the electric transmission links, by a piping diagram for pneumatic or hydraulic transmission equipment and by a simplified diagrammatic layout for mechanical linkages.
The transmission links both to and from other systems shall also be shown.
There shall be a clear correspondence between the transmission links and the signals and/or operating data carried between units.
Priorities of signals and/or operating data on multiplexed data paths shall be stated wherever priority may be an issue affecting performance or safety as far as this Regulation is concerned.
condition: wherever priority may affect performance or safety

text: Each unit of "The System" shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.
Where functions are combined within a single unit or a single computer but shown in multiple blocks in the block diagram, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used.
condition: where functions are combined within a single unit or computer

text: The manufacturer shall, by the use of the unit identification, affirm that the equipment supplied conforms to the corresponding document.

The identification shall define the hardware and software version and, where the software changes such as to alter the function of the unit as far as this Regulation is concerned, the identification shall also be changed.
condition: where the software changes so as to alter the function of the unit

text: The manufacturer shall provide a statement which affirms that the strategy chosen to achieve "The System" objectives will not, under non-fault conditions, prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle.
In respect of software employed in "The System", the outline architecture shall be explained and the design methods and tools used shall be identified.
The manufacturer shall show evidence of the means by which they determined the realisation of the system logic during the design and development process.
The manufacturer shall provide the Technical Service with an explanation of the design provisions built into "The System" so as to generate safe operation under fault conditions.
In case of a failure of "The System", the driver shall be warned, for example by warning signal or message display.

When the system is not deactivated by the driver (e.g. by turning the ignition (run) switch to "off" or by switching off that particular function with a special switch), the failure warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists.
condition: when the system is not deactivated by the driver

text: If the chosen provision selects a partial performance mode of operation under certain fault conditions, these conditions shall be stated and the resulting limits of effectiveness defined.
condition: if a partial performance mode is selected under fault conditions

text: If the chosen provision selects a second (back-up) means to realise the vehicle control system objective, the principles of the change-over mechanism, the logic and level of redundancy and any built in back-up checking features shall be explained and the resulting limits of back-up effectiveness defined.
condition: if a back-up means is selected

text: If the chosen provision selects the removal of the Higher Level Function, all the corresponding output control signals associated with this function shall be inhibited in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.
condition: if removal of the Higher Level Function is selected

text: The documentation shall be supported by an analysis which shows, in overall terms, how the system will behave on the occurrence of any individual hazard or fault which will have a bearing on vehicle control performance or safety.
The chosen analytical approach(es) shall be established and maintained by the manufacturer and shall be made open for inspection by the Technical Service at the time of the type approval.
The Technical Service shall perform an assessment of the application of the analytical approach(es).

The audit shall include inspection of the safety approach at the concept (vehicle) level with confirmation that it includes consideration of interactions with other vehicle systems, based on a Hazard / Risk analysis appropriate to system safety.

The audit shall include inspection of the safety approach at the system level, based on a Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA), a Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) or any similar process appropriate to system safety.

The audit shall include inspection of the validation plans and results, the validation using for example Hardware in the Loop (HIL) testing, vehicle on-road operational testing, or any means appropriate for validation.

The assessment shall consist of checks of hazards and faults chosen by the Technical Service to establish that the manufacturer's explanation of the safety concept is understandable, logical and that the validation plans are suitable and have been completed.

The documentation shall itemize the parameters being monitored and shall set out, for each fault condition of the type defined in paragraph 3.4.4., the warning signal to be given to the driver and/or to service/technical inspection personnel.

The documentation shall describe the measures in place to ensure "The System" does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when its performance is affected by environmental conditions, e.g. climatic, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress, ice packing.
The functional operation of "The System", as laid out in the documents required in paragraph 3, shall be tested as specified in paragraph 4.1.
The Technical Service shall verify "The System" under non-fault conditions by testing a number of selected functions from those declared by the manufacturer in paragraph 3.2.
For complex electronic systems, the verification tests shall include scenarios whereby a declared function is overridden.

The reaction of "The System" shall be checked under the influence of a failure in any individual unit by applying corresponding output signals to electrical units or mechanical elements in order to simulate the effects of internal faults within the unit.
The Technical Service shall conduct the safety concept check for at least one individual unit, but shall not check the reaction of "The System" to multiple simultaneous failures of individual units.
The Technical Service shall verify that the safety concept tests include aspects that may have an impact on vehicle controllability and user information (HMI aspects).
The verification results shall correspond with the documented summary of the failure analysis, to a level of overall effect such that the safety concept and execution are confirmed as being adequate.

Reporting of the assessment by the Technical Service shall be performed in such a manner that allows traceability, e.g. versions of documents inspected are coded and listed in the records of the Technical Service.
The false reaction scenarios of Annex 3 Appendix 2 shall be used to assess the system's strategies implemented in order to minimize the generation of false reactions.
For each type of false reaction scenario the vehicle manufacturer shall explain the principle strategies implemented to ensure safety.
The manufacturer shall provide evidence (e.g. simulation results, real-world test data, track test data) of the system's behaviour in the described types of false reaction scenarios.
The parameters described in subparagraph 2 of each false reaction scenario shall be used as guidance if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary.
condition: if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary

text: In false reaction Scenario 1 (left/right turn at the intersection in front of a stopped oncoming vehicle), the subject vehicle drives at 30 km/h (+0/-2 km/h) toward the intersection, decelerates to not less than 16 km/h where it begins to steer with TTC to the oncoming vehicle not more than 2.8 s, turns at not less than 10 km/h constant speed, and the TTC is not more than 1.7 s when the overlap ratio becomes 0 per cent; the AEBS shall minimise collision warnings and avoid emergency braking in this scenario.
condition: if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary

text: In false reaction Scenario 2 (forward vehicle turning right or left), both vehicles drive at 40 km/h (+0/-2 km/h), the forward vehicle decelerates to 10 km/h (+0/-2 km/h) to turn, the subject vehicle speed is not less than 26 km/h with TTC not more than 4.7 s when the forward vehicle begins to turn, then decelerates to not less than 20 km/h constant speed, and TTC is not more than 2.5 s when the overlap ratio becomes 0 per cent; the AEBS shall minimise collision warnings and avoid emergency braking in this scenario.
condition: if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary

text: In false reaction Scenario 3 (curved road with guard pipes and a stationary M1 vehicle, pedestrian target or bicycle target beyond the guard pipes), the subject vehicle drives at 30 km/h (+0/-2 km/h) toward a curve of radius not more than 25 m at the outer side, decelerates to not less than 22 km/h on entering the curve with TTC not more than 1.6 s, continues at a constant speed of not less than 21 km/h, and TTC is not more than 1.1 s when the overlap ratio becomes 0 per cent or the offset ratio becomes -100 per cent; the AEBS shall minimise collision warnings and avoid emergency braking in this scenario.
condition: if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary

text: In false reaction Scenario 4 (lane change due to road construction in front of a signboard in the centre of the lane), the subject vehicle drives a straight road at 40 km/h (+0/-2 km/h), begins to steer with TTC to the signboard not more than 4.2 s, keeps constant speed during the lane change, and TTC is not more than 3.3 s when the offset ratio becomes -100 per cent, with no other vehicles approaching; the AEBS shall minimise collision warnings and avoid emergency braking in this scenario.
condition: if the Technical Service deems a demonstration of the scenario necessary

text: Credibility of the toolchain used for virtual testing shall be demonstrated by the vehicle manufacturer to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service, considering the criteria capability, accuracy, correctness, fit for purpose and usability.
The virtual testing toolchain shall reflect the vehicle, system and components that are to be tested; developing and using the toolchain is the responsibility of the vehicle manufacturer.

The manufacturer shall provide to the Technical Service a description of the models and tools which constitute the toolchain and the method used to trace input data, parameters and output data back to the corresponding toolchain version.

The manufacturer shall provide to the Technical Service the processes which ensure that personnel developing, testing and validating the toolchain have appropriate experience, expertise and training, and evidence that these processes are implemented and effective.
For any toolchain activities not directly controlled by the manufacturer, an explanation of measures taken to ensure confidence in the quality and integrity of these activities shall be provided.
condition: if there are activities not directly controlled by the manufacturer

text: The manufacturer shall provide a description of the input parameters, along with any uncertainties in the model parameters, used to validate the models included in the tools and toolchain.
The manufacturer shall provide documentation demonstrating that the data used to validate the models covers the intended scope and functionality of the toolchain.
The manufacturer shall provide a description of the overall approach to data management for the toolchain.

The manufacturer shall provide a description of the management activities covering modifications between toolchain releases, version control and the review processes ensuring modifications result in a toolchain that is still suitable.
All parts of the toolchain, tools and models shall be described by the manufacturer.

The vehicle manufacturer shall define the validity domain on which the toolchain will be applicable and how it has been derived, including any AEBS performance influencing factors, parameter ranges, assumptions, limitations and tolerances.
The toolchain documentation shall include a description of the key performance indicators to be assessed during validation, such as time to collision, remaining distance or impact speed.
The toolchain documentation shall include a description of the accuracy requirements for the toolchain and its components, including comparison with physical tests.
The documentation of the toolchain shall include assumptions, limitations, uncertainties and the necessary levels of fidelity.

The manufacturer shall provide a description of the toolchain assessment methodology, including the impact of any errors and uncertainties on the results and the consequences for the compliance of the system with this Regulation.
The manufacturer shall review the information produced in defining the validity domain (paragraph 2.3.6.2.) and document any implications for the use of the toolchain.
The toolchain and its components shall be capable of accurately representing the relevant aspects of the physical AEBS that is being modelled.

The manufacturer shall provide documentation on the verification activity of the modelling that implements the AEBS function in the toolchain, including a description of the models, their implementation, how they represent the AEBS function and the activities performed to confirm correct implementation.
The manufacturer shall provide an estimation of the numerical errors affecting the toolchain and its components and analysis that the errors remain sufficiently bounded.

The manufacturer shall demonstrate the effect of variations of the model parameters on the output values and identify the most critical parameters influencing the results, including a robust calibration procedure for these parameters.
The vehicle manufacturer shall describe their overall approach to validation including performance measures and a validation strategy.

The validation strategy shall be agreed by the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service, including physical tests performed to demonstrate that the toolchain is an accurate representation of the physical system.
The validation tests performed shall ensure that a statistical comparison between physical and simulation results is possible.
The validation strategy shall be defined by the manufacturer and presented to the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service for review and agreement.

The manufacturer shall demonstrate how the toolchain achieves the defined key performance indicators and accuracy requirements, including justification for their choice and the criteria for satisfying them.
The manufacturer shall provide the list of validation scenarios.
The manufacturer shall provide the parameter descriptions and accuracy requirements needed to perform the validation tests.

The manufacturer shall provide documentation describing the validation performed to establish the credibility of the toolchain, including the processes followed, physical tests performed and models and tools used.
The manufacturer shall provide documentation demonstrating how they have characterised the uncertainty in the input data and evaluated the model parameters.

The overall uncertainty of the virtual testing results shall be quantified based on the toolchain structure and the data and its flow through the toolchain, allowing estimates of likely errors and required safety margins.
The required safety margins derived from the uncertainty quantification shall be applied to the results when the toolchain is used for virtual testing.

At the request of the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service, additional confirmatory validation including physical tests shall be performed or witnessed, relevant to the entire toolchain, specific parts or any of its components.
condition: at the request of the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service

text: The number of physical validation tests shall be defined in agreement between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service.
The physical validation tests shall be sufficient to cover the validity domain specified by the vehicle manufacturer.

The methodology used to generate physical validation data, such as data recording equipment, data processing and calculation of scalar values, shall be documented as part of the validation documentation.

Compliance of the AEBS with the performance requirements of paragraphs 5.2.1 to 5.2.3 may be demonstrated by the vehicle manufacturer to the Type Approval Authority or its Technical Service by virtual testing of the dynamic manoeuvres described in paragraphs 6.4. to 6.7.
condition: at the request of the vehicle manufacturer, where virtual testing is used

text: All virtual testing results provided by the manufacturer in applying for an approval shall refer to the toolchain evaluated and validated according to this annex.
For each approval application the manufacturer shall provide a confirmation that the virtual testing was conducted using a validated toolchain.
For each approval application the manufacturer shall provide a confirmation that the virtual testing was performed by staff with appropriate competences and skills.

For each approval application the manufacturer shall provide a confirmation that the virtual testing has been performed using a toolchain that has a unique identifier and sufficient information including scope, regulatory applicability and validation history to ensure traceability and assurance that the toolchain is suitable and fit for purpose.
For each approval application the manufacturer shall provide a confirmation that the virtual testing has been performed using a toolchain within its scope and in accordance with any restrictions.
